text: An orbit that goes around the Earth 8.05 times a day with an eccentricity of 0.25 (the exact 8:1 resonance with the Earth's rotation) is predicted 1.3 km off along its track 7 days after a fit, against 94 to 220 m just either side of it: no part of the model carries that resonance's gravity terms.

On seven real windows of the TESS space telescope (an orbit of 13.7 days that reaches the Moon's distance) the median prediction error is 1.01 km after one day and 9.0 km after a week, above the earlier record of 0.77 and 7.6 km, and AP is 706 m behind SGP4-XP at day 3 (the bound is 50 m). The numerical propagator fitted and scored the same way is 0.48 km off after one day and 1.6 km after three. AP's output on that orbit is now in the right frame: with every force but radiation it follows the numerical propagator to 37 m in a week, where the frame's error was 1.8 km. The frame's error had partly offset AP's radiation pressure on that orbit: a 72-hour fit follows the numerical propagator's radiation pressure no closer than 46 to 174 m, and it misses by 1.5 to 7 km five days later.

On a 7-day arc of an eccentric orbit with drag (Molniya), the record states the drag coefficient to 0.09 % while the fitted value is 0.3 to 0.5 % from the truth: the stated uncertainty is 5 to 7 times too small; its position covariance is honest.
